questions.q: What is the exact problem this lesson says a semantic layer solves?
options: The same metric (like "revenue") getting defined differently in every BI tool that touches the same underlying data
Warehouses being too slow to run any query
dbt models having no version control
SQL syntax differing between warehouses
questions.explain: Even against the same clean marts model, different tools can each define "revenue" differently — the semantic layer moves that definition to one place everyone shares.

questions.q: What is MetricFlow's actual job, according to this lesson?
options: It compiles a metric's definition, at query time, into the correct SQL for whatever is actually being asked
It replaces the need for a data warehouse entirely
It is a BI tool that competes with Tableau and Power BI
It only formats numbers for display, with no query logic
questions.explain: MetricFlow is the query engine that turns one metric definition into the right SQL for different queries — by month, by region, etc.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is the dbt Semantic Layer a real, connectable feature or just a conceptual idea?
options: It's real — dbt Cloud exposes an actual Environment ID, Host, JDBC URL, and GraphQL URL that BI tools connect to
It's purely conceptual with no real implementation
It only exists as a marketing diagram with no working endpoint
It requires writing a custom API from scratch for every BI tool
questions.explain: The lesson shows a real dbt Cloud connection panel with working connection details a BI tool actually uses.

questions.q: What clue from Lesson 1's file-explorer screenshot does this lesson point to as indirect proof MetricFlow is a real, current dbt feature?
options: A real file named metricflow_time_spine.sql sitting in that dbt project
A folder named 'semantic' with no files in it
A comment in the README mentioning MetricFlow
There was no such clue in Lesson 1
questions.explain: Lesson 1's screenshot showed a real metricflow_time_spine.sql file — MetricFlow needs a date spine to calculate time-based metrics.

questions.q: Once a metric is defined once in dbt's semantic layer, what happens when different BI tools query it?
options: They all get the identical calculation, because they're asking the same semantic layer the same question instead of writing their own SQL
Each tool still calculates its own separate answer
Only one BI tool at a time is allowed to connect
The metric definition is copied and hardcoded into each tool separately
questions.explain: Every connected tool queries the same semantic layer, so they all get the same answer instead of re-deriving their own logic.
